messages:
alex.k: Heads-up — I'm kicking off an apples-to-apples comparison of the embedding->rerank flow. Goal: isolate batching, vector dim, and payload-size effects on tail latency (p95/p99). Planning synthetic and replay runs in the same infra.

maria.s: Nice. Which endpoints and models?

alex.k: Two endpoints: /embed (batching allowed) -> store vectors; /rerank (online, batched scoring). Models: open-embed-1536-v1 and open-embed-768-v2 to compare dims. Sequence: 1) synthetic generator with configurable payload size, 2) replay harness using real traffic from last week's rerank logs.

sahil: Are we controlling for kernel selection? I want the comparison to force the same kernel family where possible. Recent kernel selector change caused p99 spikes.

alex.k: Yes — experiment matrix includes: (A) default kernel selection, (B) force fused-attn kernel, (C) force generic kernel. We pin CUDA/cuDNN versions and quantization bits. We'll run each config 3x and report median.

carol: For the replay runs: use exact same request ordering and concurrency as live? or replay with concurrency shaping?

alex.k: We replay two modes: "1:1 replay" which preserves inter-arrival times, and "burst-replay" where we scale QPS by 2x/5x to stress batching heuristics. Both run on a dedicated-node pool to avoid noisy neighbors.

bench-bot: Command to run harness: `./harness/replay --input s3://redwood/rerank-logs/2026-03-01.gz --mode burst --qps 200 --keyspace session_id --preserve-order`

maria.s: Nice. Can you paste the config you're using for payload sizes? Small metadata-only vs large context?

alex.k: Config snippet:
```
{
  "embed_payload": [128, 512, 2048],
  "rerank_doc_len": [64, 512],
  "vector_dim": [1536, 768],
  "batch_window_ms": [1, 5, 20],
  "concurrency": [16, 64]
}
```

carol: We should also track KV-cache hit-rate for rerank cases where there's repeated prefixes — might reduce compute. Include KV metrics.

alex.k: Added. KV warmup: cold vs warm runs. We'll run warm path with a priming phase to populate prefix/kvcache.

ev an.p: (typo) evan.p: Also log kernel-selection traces + nvtx and perf counters. If p99 regresses, we need flamegraphs to see whether it's kernel or scheduling.

bench-bot: Reminder: ensure `REPRO_PIN=1` to pin model binary and disable auto-upgrade of kernel selection.

maria.s: For apples-to-apples we need the same model weights and tokenizer binary across runs. Use s3://redwood/models/open-embed-1536-v1/sha256:abcd1234 for the 1536 model.

alex.k: Using that. Results from first small run (summary):
- config: vector=1536, batch_window=5ms, concurrency=16, kernel=default, replay=1:1
- p50 embed: 12ms, p95: 42ms, p99: 110ms
- p50 rerank: 18ms, p95: 85ms, p99: 210ms
- kv-cache cold -> warm delta: rerank p99 improved ~25% after warmup

maria.s: Those p99s for rerank look high. Do you have CPU vs GPU breakdown?

alex.k: Yes — tracer shows GPU token loop is fine; the big chunk is CPU-side batching window and serialization when payloads are larger (2048). For payload=2048 we see a 2.3x tail increase due to serialization blocking the networking thread.

sahil: That matches the kernel-selector regression I saw — fallback to generic kernel increases GPU per-token time and pushes more work to GPU, which increases queueing and exacerbates CPU serialization waits.

carol: Any reproducible perf regression relative to baseline (two weeks ago)?

alex.k: Compared to baseline (1747000000 run): same binary, but we changed the kernel-selection heuristics. Baseline rerank p99 was ~120ms. New selection -> 210ms in worst case. Repro steps attached below.

evan.p: Please attach the profile. We need NVTX ranges and a `perf script` stack to see where time is spent.

alex.k: Pasted the stripped logs: 
```
[PROFILE] GPU kernels: fused-attn: 62%, generic-attn: 33%, softmax: 5%
[TRACE] CPU: serialization: 45ms, batching-window-wait: 12ms, network-io: 8ms
[FLAME] top: io_thread -> serialize_payload -> send_batch -> wait_for_gpu
```

maria.s: So mitigations? Short-term: reduce batch_window_ms to 1ms for rerank endpoint to cut serialization wait. Medium: optimize serialization path (zero-copy headers) and ensure kernel selector prefers fused-attn for these shapes.

sahil: Also worth instrumenting batch composition distribution (how many vectors per GPU batch) and track effective utilization. If single huge payloads crowd out many small requests, tail suffers.

alex.k: Agreed. Next runs: 1) batch_window=1ms + pinned fused-attn 2) batch_window=20ms + force generic 3) replay burst 5x with mixed vector dims.

bench-bot: Job queued: run_id=rerank-fidelity-1748573290-1, target_pool=dedicated-gpu-large, notify=#eng-runtime on complete

carol: When you publish results, include CSV with columns: run_id, vector_dim, payload_bytes, batch_size_mean, batch_size_p95, p50_ms, p95_ms, p99_ms, kv_hit_rate, kernel_family. That makes apples-to-apples comparisons easy.

alex.k: Will do. One more note: we saw memory copy overhead when vector_dim=1536 with payloads >1KB; enabling pinned host buffers reduced p99 by ~18% in a microbench. I'll include that flag in a follow-up test.

maria.s: Thanks — keep the thread updated. If anyone wants to join the live run at 14:00 PT ping me and I'll open a debug terminal. :eyes:

sahil: I'll watch kernel traces. :chart_with_upwards_trend:

carol: Thanks — let's prioritize the fused-attn pin for rerank if it reproduces lower p99. :thumbsup:

alex.k: Done for the first pass. I'll upload full CSV + flamegraphs to s3://redwood/bench/rerank-fidelity/1748573290/ once jobs finish.
